@graph.name: Plate Reader Endpoint Assay Workflow
@graph.description: A metadata-driven R workflow for processing endpoint colorimetric and fluorescence assays from 96-well microplate readers. Parses raw instrument exports (SpectraMax iD3 or BioTek Synergy 2) or a user-prepared .xlsx file for any other instrument, subtracts blanks, fits a linear standard curve, back-calculates sample concentrations (flagging out-of-range samples as extrapolated rather than dropping them), and exports plate-map, standard-curve, and sample-value plots and CSVs.

@graph.name: SpectraMax endpoint assay pipeline
@graph.description: Parses SpectraMax iD3 SDA endpoint-assay exports (.csv, .xls, or .txt), auto-detecting absorbance vs. fluorescence read mode and the measured wavelength(s), including multi-wavelength absorbance exports. Subtracts blank signal, evaluates the assay's signal formula, fits a linear standard curve, and back-calculates sample concentrations. See examples/example_run_amplexred/ (Amplex Red H2O2, fluorescence), examples/example_run_bradford_legacy/ (real two-wavelength Bradford data), and examples/example_run_format_consistency/ (cross-format equivalence audit) for runnable demonstrations.

@graph.name: BioTek Synergy 2 endpoint assay pipeline
@graph.description: The same pipeline as process_spectramax_endpoint_std_curve.R, adapted for BioTek Synergy 2 Gen5 .xlsx exports. Only raw-file parsing differs between the two scripts; blank correction, signal formula, standard curve, plotting, and outputs are identical. See examples/example_run/ (BCA, real data) for a runnable demonstration. Note: multi-wavelength Synergy2 support is implemented but not verified against a real multi-wavelength Synergy2 export (none available) — see examples/example_run_format_consistency/ and CHANGELOG.md [1.1.0] for this known limitation.

@graph.name: Generic Excel endpoint assay pipeline
@graph.description: The same pipeline as process_spectramax_endpoint_std_curve.R, but reads a user-prepared .xlsx file instead of an instrument-specific export, for use with any plate reader. Auto-detects a long format (single sheet, columns well/wavelength/signal) or a plate format (one 8x12-grid sheet per wavelength, sheet name = wavelength) from the first sheet's cell A1. Only raw-file parsing differs from the other two scripts; blank correction, signal formula, standard curve, plotting, and outputs are identical. See examples/example_run_generic_excel/ (fabricated, both formats), examples/example_run_bradford_legacy/ (real data, plate format), examples/example_run_tgsh_legacy/ (real data, long format), and examples/example_run_format_consistency/ (cross-format equivalence audit) for runnable demonstrations.

@graph.name: BCA (absorbance, real data) example run
@graph.description: Complete, runnable example against real data: a genuine BCA protein assay exported from a BioTek Synergy 2 (2026.06.15), six in-range samples. This is the only example that exercises process_synergy2_endpoint_std_curve.R, and the only one whose sample_dil_final is left to the pipeline's own auto-calculation rather than being set explicitly. Includes raw instrument export, exp_metadata CSV, and the expected processed outputs (plate map, summary PDF, levels CSV, analytical performance CSV).

@graph.name: Amplex Red (fluorescence) example run
@graph.description: Complete, runnable example against fabricated SpectraMax fluorescence data. Demonstrates smp_blk matrix-matched blank wells and extrapolation flagging: one sample's signal is deliberately above the top standard and is back-calculated but flagged extrapolated = TRUE rather than dropped.

@graph.name: Generic Excel input example run (both formats)
@graph.description: Runs process_generic_excel_endpoint_std_curve.R against the same fabricated two-wavelength (A412 - A700) assay data encoded twice: once as a long-format .xlsx and once as a plate-format .xlsx. Asserts both back-calculate to the same sample concentrations, demonstrating the two input formats are equivalent.

@graph.name: Bradford (legacy, real data) example run
@graph.description: Runs process_generic_excel_endpoint_std_curve.R against real data (not fabricated) from a 2024 Bradford protein assay, reorganized from its original SpectraMax export into the generic-Excel plate format. Demonstrates a two-wavelength ratio signal formula (A590/A450) and adapting an older exp_metadata/assay_metadata layout to the current schema without altering recorded values.

@graph.name: tGSH (legacy, real data) example run
@graph.description: Runs process_generic_excel_endpoint_std_curve.R against real data from a 2024 total-glutathione enzymatic recycling assay, reorganized into the generic-Excel long format. Real, not fabricated, data (see examples/example_run_bradford_legacy/ for the plate-format counterpart). The original export omitted blank-well readings entirely; the confirmed real value (0.000) is encoded explicitly rather than left undefined.

@graph.name: Cross-format consistency audit example run
@graph.description: Proves the workflow produces identical back-calculated results regardless of raw-file format and wavelength count. Two canonical datasets, each re-encoded into every format with a trustworthy reference structure: the real single-wavelength BCA data from examples/example_run/ across all four formats (Synergy2, SpectraMax, generic-Excel long, generic-Excel plate), and the fabricated two-wavelength ABTS data from examples/example_run_generic_excel/ across three (generic-Excel long, generic-Excel plate, SpectraMax). Deliberately excludes a two-wavelength Synergy2 leg, since no real multi-wavelength Synergy2 export exists to verify that raw-file layout against.
